jobs.description:
"You care about making a positive impact in the world. You understand greatness requires thinking differently. An inclusive and accepting work environment is important to you.

A job at IKEA is so much more than home furnishings. Together, we work to make a better everyday life for the many. It's the perfect fit if you want to contribute, grow, and share. Join the team and start a better life for yourself."

Candidate profile

We will love you for your openness and willingness to meet our customer! We have high expectations of our co-workers and you can expect to be delegated a big reasonability. You thrive in meeting our customer with a smile and positive attitude, you flourish in a busy work environment with a lot of customers and colleagues around. You have an eye for details to make sure the store always looks inviting. Furthermore, you should be prepared to sometimes do physical hard labor.

We believe that we, with our different backgrounds and competences, can reach even further – common for us all is that we thrive to create a better everyday life for the many people.

Key responsibilities

At IKEA we offer a variety of jobs and maybe there is one that suits you:

Sales: We are divided into three main areas; Showroom, home accessories and Tá selv lageret. Common to all three areas is that we guide and advise our customers, so that they come home with exactly the product that makes their everyday life better.

We therefore emphasize that you:

• Have experience with sales and customer service, possibly experience from furniture sales or other types of consideration purchases

• Thrive on guiding customers in a busy everyday life, are motivated by active sales and creating a good shopping experience

• Take responsibility for prioritizing your own work tasks so that time is utilized most efficiently

• Are able to approach tasks with a structured and goal-oriented mind

• Have a good physique and thrive on physically hard work

• Can speak Danish.

Customer service: Here we always have the customer in mind, regardless of whether we are in the checkout, småland, handout or return department. We have a daily dialogue with many different customers, for which we make sure that all customers have a good experience and leave the store with a smile on their face.

We therefore emphasize that you:

• Are outgoing with a positive energy and can put yourself in the customers' place - even in pressured situations

• Can keep calm and collective and communicate clearly with our customers

• Thrive with routines, are thorough and have an eye for detail

• Have a good physique and thrives with physically hard work

• Are good at numbers, IT and a skilled problem solver

• Can speak Danish.

IKEA FOOD: The food at IKEA must always be of good quality. We pride ourselves on the food that we serve in the restaurant and bistro always is perceived as inspiring and delicious – at a reasonable price. We meet our customers every day at the checkout or serving station, we prepare both hot and cold dishes and make sure that our customers always have clean service to eat from.

We favor that you:

• Have experience from the restaurant-, fast-food- or retail business

• Thrive in a physical hard job

• Can meet our customers with a positive attitude in a busy work environment

• Are motivated by teamwork and reaching our goals as a team

• Have a sense of order and understand the importance of complying with various standards in restaurant operation.

LOGISTIC: We work primarily at night and in the early morning hours, where we ensure to restock the shelfs with goods in our store. As a logistic co-worker you play a big part in our sales figures and customer experience. You help our customers not to go in vain when they are buying new furniture or accessories for their home. We have a busy work environment and a strict deadline - the store opening.

We prefer that you:

• Have experience as warehouse co-worker and/or hard manual labor in a fast-paced and changeable environment

• Thrive with shifting work hours – including working at night

• Are motivated by prioritizing and organizing your own work to make efficient use of time

• Are good at communicating in English and enthusiastic about working in a team

• Have a license for operating forklift trucks or the desire to require one.

Together as a team

If you are looking for a place with good colleagues and a strong unity, there is room for you at IKEA. Together we work to fulfill the interior design dreams and create a better everyday life for the many people who visit us every day. Here you can both start your career and gain study-relevant experience. You will gain knowledge on how a large international company operates, and there is room for your strengths and for you to develop your career. We help each other, and together we create the good atmosphere in IKEA. Here there is room for those who are focused and those who love to change plans. There is room for you.

Let's connect

If you have any questions, please email us on recruitment.pc.dk@ingka.ikea.com. Please notice that we do not receive application via E-mail but only through our recruitment portal.

WHAT ELSE TO EXPECT

With a part-time job at IKEA your working hours will primarily be planed for the evenings at weekdays and every other weekend (Logistic as an exception).

In a full-time job your working hours will be planned in and around the opening hours of the store. You can expect to work 1-2 evenings pr. week and every other weekend.

You will be able to provide your inputs for your coming work schedule and will know you work schedule for 16 weeks at a time. With a job at IKEA follows a list of benefits such as:

• Pension and health insurance

• Massage

• Co-worker discount

• Bonus programme etc.

We offer a salary within union agreement with HK (IKEA Food follows the union agreement with 3F cafeteria), and we will provide you with work clothes and safety shoes. We process incoming applications ongoing.

Why you will love us

From the deep forests in Sweden, we have spread our culture and values around the world. At the heart of our offer are our beautiful home-furnishing products and solutions, made with care for our planet, reaching millions of customers.

At the heart of our business, are our wonderful co-workers representing diversity in all dimensions and passionate for life at home. We all contribute with our uniqueness and we want to grow and develop together.

Our vision, “to create a better everyday life for the many people” inspires and guides us in everything we do. This is IKEA.

What we all have in common

• Living our values

• Being your unique self, while respecting and including others

• A passion for home furnishing

• Performing & delivering while learning & developing

• Having fun!

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowship in Social Sciences with a focus on Economics of the Health Care Sector and Circular Economy
jobs.description:
The Department of Social Sciences and Business (ISE), Roskilde University, invites applications for a position as PhD fellow as part of a large interdisciplinary research project anchored at the Department for Science and Environment (INM) but which is undertaken in collaboration with ISE. The position is from March 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter and is limited to a period of 3 years.

The project
The PhD Fellow will be hired under the newly initiated interdisciplinary and collaborative research project ROUNDS: Rethinking the cost of care – including the cost of externalities in circular transitions funded under TRACE - A Path to Resilience, and the Innovation Fund Denmark. ROUNDS is a partnership between Roskilde University, Gate21, University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University, and two Danish regions Region Sjælland (soon: Region East) and Region Midtjylland.

Background
Danish hospitals rely heavily on single-use plastics and textiles, a reliance reinforced by procurement practices primarily built around unit price rather than the full cost of a product across its lifecycle. Hidden health and environmental costs - negative externalities such as those associated with PFAS-treated textiles and PVC-based plastics - are rarely reflected in what hospitals pay. This keeps safer, more circular alternatives at an apparent price disadvantage even where they are preferable on a full-cost basis. Addressing this mismatch is central to enabling a circular transition in healthcare. ROUNDS addresses these issues by combining evidence on negative externalities, procurement evaluation, and behavioural strategies. Furthermore, the project will deliver strategic research addressing two key drivers of single-use plastics and textiles consumption by generating knowledge on health and environmental effects and using these insights to inform economic assessments for procurement, and staff training and collaboration to influence behaviour.

Description of the PhD project
The aim of the PhD project, which is embedded in ROUNDS, is to produce applicable, scientific knowledge on how negative externalities can be identified, valued, and integrated into public procurement practices in the healthcare sector. The project will challenge established economic processes for public procurement by applying environmental and ecological economics concepts and methods to suitably value product types. Based on multi-criteria evaluation, the PhD will develop and pilot-test a procurement framework that accounts for health and environmental externalities alongside conventional cost criteria, anchored empirically in two cases: the transition from single-use PFAS-containing surgical gowns to reusable alternatives, and the substitution and reduction of PVC-based single-use infusion sets. Pilot testing with regional procurement teams will validate usability and feasibility in real-world settings.

The PhD project involves four main activities/tasks:

• Mapping current procurement practices: Documenting how procurement decisions for the project's two healthcare case products (single-use PFAS surgical gowns and PVC infusion sets) are currently made and identifying the structural and economic barriers that keep negative externalities out of the calculation.
• Developing a valuation methodology: multi-criteria evaluation to build a methodology for including health- and environmental externalities in the economic assessment of healthcare products beyond single monetary metrics, in dialogue with the project's human health risk assessment work.
• Stakeholder and market dialogue: Engaging procurement and finance departments in the participating regions, and relevant industry and supplier representatives, to test the practical relevance and feasibility of the emerging framework.
• Applying and pilot-testing the procurement framework: Applying the developed framework to the project's two cases and, together with regional procurement teams, pilot-testing its usability in real-world settings, contributing to a final guide for economic valuation and circular public procurement.

Considerations regarding how to work with the four main activities listed above must be included in your project description. The activities may be adjusted and defined in more details in the PhD plan that is to be developed by the PhD candidate, in collaboration with the supervisors, during the first three months of the PhD project.

The PhD Fellow will be a part of the International Section at ISE, where the main supervisor is based, but will also become embedded at INM to gain deeper insights into the ROUNDS project and benefit from co-supervision by an interdisciplinary environmental scientist.

The Doctoral School
You will be enrolled as a PhD fellow at the Doctoral School of Social Sciences and Business with approximately 47 PhD fellows from all over the world.

The Doctoral School of Social Sciences & Business provides PhD training and research within an interdisciplinary, international, and professional environment. It is part of a dynamic community of researchers who share a commitment to understanding society in diverse contexts of change and global engagement. Researchers come from all over the world and engage in topics that are geographically, theoretically and methodologically diverse. The Doctoral School has one PhD programme. The programme offers work-in-progress seminars, thematic professional development seminars, feedback and social activities for enrolled PhD fellows. As a PhD fellow you will be part of the STEPUP research group and affiliated with the Plastics research team at INM.

Responsibilities and tasks
As a PhD fellow you are trained at an international level to undertake research. You are responsible for carrying out independent research under supervision and receiving constructive feedback in the PhD programme to finish your PhD thesis. During your employment you are required to take 30 ECTS of coursework, and gain experience in teaching and supervision. You are also required to have a research environmental change during your PhD enrollment. The environment change can take place at foreign or local universities or research institutions.

For more information, see chapter 3, Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. Read more on what it entails to be a PhD Fellow at Roskilde University.

Qualifications
You must hold a master’s degree or equivalent in economics or a field relevant to the topic, for instance, environmental and sustainability sciences.

Qualifications within the following areas are required:

• Strong analytical skills and research potential
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; Danish is an asset.
• Advanced methodological skills both quantitative and qualitative/mixed-method
• Experience with conducting both surveys and qualitative interviews
• Ability to work within a larger project team across disciplines

Relevant knowledge about plastics obtained either from educational background (courses, project work etc.) or from work related experiences is an asset. Moreover, you are required to be enterprising and to possess good communication skills and to be a visible, involved participant in the Department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Applications are invited from both inside and outside Denmark.

Assessment
In the assessment regarding employment consideration will be given to:

• Relevant master’s degree or equivalent (according to Danish Qualifications Framework for Higher Education)
• Any additional academic requirements stated in the job advertisement.

In the assessment regarding enrollment consideration will also be given to the following criteria:

• Educational skills and any further professional qualifications within the social sciences.
• Grades at a social science master’s program or equivalent.
• Quality and relevance of the project description.
• Quality and relevance of the methodical and theoretical choices.
• Consistency and coherence between the problem and the choice of method and theory.
• If the PhD project seem realistic and feasible
• Ability to complete the PhD project.
• Relevance of the project to the profile of the Doctoral School.
• Your project description shall be no more than 5 pages (excluding references).

Questions
For further information about the position, please contact Head of the PhD school Lena Brogaard (brogaard@ruc.dk). For technical or administrative questions, please contact the PhD Administration (hr-phdadmin@ruc.dk).

Terms of employment
The employment is full time, 37 hours per week and you will refer to the Head of Department.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. 

According to the Pay Transparency Directive, the salary ranges for the various job categories at Roskilde University are listed here. 

Application procedure

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application

Only applications in English are accepted.

4. Your description of the PhD project (no more than 5 pages)

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in corporate networks and computational social science
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School, Department of Organization invites applications for a vacant Postdoc in corporate networks and computational social science

Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoctoral position associated with the CLONE project (Consequences of Long-term Organizational Embeddedness). The position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of corporate network analysis, computational social science, economic sociology, and large-scale research infrastructure.

The CLONE project studies the structure and transformation of corporate networks and the organizations and individuals that constitute them. A central ambition of the project is to develop data infrastructure that makes it possible to analyse corporate networks systematically and to connect network structures to firms' economic characteristics, activities, and representations of themselves.

The successful candidate will play a central role in developing, analysing, and making accessible the project's corporate network data. The position combines independent research with collaborative data development and provides considerable opportunities for developing new research using a unique combination of network, accounting, and textual data. Examples of research areas that the Postdoc might cover:

• Corporate networks and elite structures
• Corporate data infrastructure and research databases
• Computational analysis of annual reports and other corporate texts
The Postdoc is a non-tenured position for a one-year period with research obligation.

To fulfill the research requirements of the position, the applicant chosen is expected to be physically present on a regular basis and actively participate in the teaching and research activities of the Department.

Qualifications
The applicant must hold a PhD or the equivalent. In assessing applications, particular emphasis will be placed on research potential.

Emphasis is placed on research relevant to the job description.

The ideal candidate has strong quantitative and computational skills, with experience in social network analysis and large-scale data management. Experience with corporate, accounting or textual data, record linkage, and programming in R, Python or related tools is an advantage. Knowledge of the CLONE database and historical developments of Danish corporate networks is key to be able to fulfill the tasks of the position.

The applicant must have professional proficiency in English (written and spoken).

Copenhagen Business School has a broad commitment to the excellence, distinctiveness and relevance of its teaching and research programmes.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Responsible AI in Software Engineering Education
jobs.description:
The Center for Industrial Software (CIS) at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Møller Institute, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD position in Responsible AI in Software Engineering Education. The position is based at SDU’s campus in Sønderborg and is available from 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position is funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and is part of PREPARE — Pedagogical Alignment for Responsible AI in Software Engineering Education, a joint project between SDU and the IT University of Copenhagen (ITU).

CIS is a young but fast-growing unit whose research groups span cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, embedded systems, and software engineering. Our students and staff come from Denmark, the rest of the EU, and beyond, and our working language is English.

 

About the position

Generative AI has arrived in our classrooms faster than our pedagogy has adapted to it. Students increasingly delegate the very things we are trying to teach them — verification, trade-off reasoning, judgment, accountability — to tools whose reasoning they cannot inspect. Most institutional responses so far have been restrictions or isolated policies, and neither addresses the underlying problem. This project takes the opposite route: if AI is here to stay in software engineering practice, responsible AI use should be deliberately taught, practiced, and assessed.

This is a unique position in that research and its consequences sit in the same place. You will not be studying a distant phenomenon and writing it up; you will be running studies in live courses, designing interventions from what you find, and seeing them change how software engineering is taught. If you see yourself as someone who wants to help our discipline navigate the AI disruption rather than wait for it to settle, this is that opportunity.

 

Responsibility and opportunities

Concretely, you can expect to:

• 
Design and conduct empirical studies of how software engineering students generally use generative AI — how they justify it, what they delegate to it, and where their agency is preserved or surrendered.

• 
Translate those findings into agency artifacts, practicum activities, and assessment designs that can be used by real instructors in real courses.

• 
Co-develop and evaluate self-learning components, and contribute to alignment work on intended learning outcomes, activities, and assessment together with the ITU stream.

• 
Work directly with the head of programs and instructors to implement classroom interventions, whose buy-in is what makes this kind of change hold. Persuading colleagues is part of the craft here, not an afterthought.

• 
Publish in leading venues for computing education research, and present internationally.

 

Required scientific qualifications

• 
A master’s degree in software engineering, computer science, or a closely related field, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree and including a substantial thesis component. The degree must be completed before the starting date. Students with master’s in education and related fields are welcome to apply.

• 
A grade average at or above 10 on the Danish 7-point scale, or a documented equivalent from the awarding institution. Applicants with degrees from outside Denmark should include a grading scale and, where available, a conversion statement.

• 
Documented ability to carry out independent scientific work, evidenced by the master’s thesis.

 

Qualifications

Required

• 
A software engineering background, with practical familiarity with how software is actually built — you should be able to judge whether an AI-assisted solution is sound, not only whether it runs.

• 
A genuine motivation for teaching and education, both in delivery and as an object of research.

• 
The ability to design and carry out empirical studies involving students, and to engage stakeholders for support.

• 
Excellent written and spoken English.

Nice to have

• 
Prior research and publication experience.

• 
Experience with empirical research methods — interventions, experiment, interviews, coding, thematic or pattern analysis — and with mixed-methods designs.

• 
Familiarity with computing education research, or with constructive alignment as a course design framework.

• 
Teaching or teaching-assistant experience at university level.

• 
Hands-on experience using generative AI tools in software development, and a considered view of where they help and where they do not.

 

Personal competences

• 
Critical and ingenious thinking. You question assumptions — including your own, including ours, and including the ones embedded in our education design and the AI tools you will be studying. You are as interested in what a finding does not show as in what it does.

• 
A demonstrated passion for software engineering and its education. This project asks you to care about how the next generation of engineers is formed, not only about publishing on the topic.

• 
The ability to bring colleagues along. Much of this work happens through instructors and program leaderships who own their courses. We value someone who can earn agreement through evidence, patience, and good listening rather than argument alone.

• 
Independence paired with collaboration. You will drive your own studies, and you will do it inside a two-university project with shared deliverables and deadlines.

• 
Integrity and care in working with students. You will be researching people who are also being taught and assessed. That asymmetry has to be handled thoughtfully.

• 
Comfort with iteration. Design-based research means your first intervention will be wrong in interesting ways. That is the method working, not failing.

 

Workplace description

The Center for Industrial Software (CIS) is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Møller Institute at SDU’s Faculty of Engineering. We are a young unit that has grown quickly, with close ties to industry in the region. We take our international workplace seriously.

You will be based at SDU’s campus in Sønderborg, sitting on the strait that separates the island of Als from the mainland. Sønderborg is a coastal town of around 27,000 in a municipality of 76,000, built around an 800-year-old castle and shaped by its position on the Danish–German border. It is small enough to cross by bike and rich enough in coastline, forest, and cultural life that people who come for a few years often stay longer. The international community is sizeable, thanks to the university and the global companies based nearby, and Copenhagen is a 35-minute flight or a direct train away. Two good starting points: VisitSønderborg for the area itself, and Hej Sønderborg, an English-language blog written for newcomers about living here.

 

Further information about the position contact Associate Professor Adam Alami, at adal@mmmi.sdu.dk.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Two recommendation letters, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation). 

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Class, Elites and the Political Economy of the Green Transition – BACKLASH Project
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School, Department of Organization invites applications for a postdoctoral position associated with the research project “BACKLASH: Social Inequality and Democratic Sustainability in the Green Transition”.

BACKLASH investigates how social and economic inequalities shape support for and resistance to climate policy in Denmark. The overarching research question is: How do social and economic class dynamics structure support for and resistance to climate policy in Denmark?

A central concept in the project is the climate-political class landscape, which combines actors’ positions in the economic hierarchy with their structural dependence on either fossil-based economic activities or the green transition. BACKLASH uses this framework to investigate potential alliances and conflicts between different class positions and between “green” and “fossil” fractions of capital and other social groups.

The successful candidate will take a leading role in the project’s quantitative research and will work at the intersection of class analysis, elite studies, political economy, climate politics and relational quantitative methods.

Examples of research areas that the Postdoc might cover:

• Class, inequality and the political economy of the green transition
• Elite and organizational networks
• Relational quantitative methods and emissions inequality
The Postdoc is a non-tenured position for a two-year period with research obligation.

To fulfill the research requirements of the position, the applicant chosen is expected to be physically present on a regular basis and actively participate in the activities of the Department.

Qualifications
The applicant must hold a PhD or the equivalent. In assessing applications, particular emphasis will be placed on research potential.

Emphasis is placed on research relevant to the job description.

The applicant should have strong quantitative methodological skills, particularly in relational quantitative methods such as social network analysis and multiple correspondence analysis. We particularly welcome candidates with knowledge of the political economy of the green transition and a strong interest in social class, inequality and elites. Experience with survey analysis, emissions data, text analysis or large-scale data integration is an advantage.

The applicant must have professional proficiency in English (written and spoken).

jobs.occupation: Staff scientist in the Human Organoid facility at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Vaccines and Immunity
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI Research) seeks a staff scientist to join the Human Immune Organoids facility for a position of 3 years. The position will be available 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  NIVI Research is embedded in the Department of Immunology and Microbiology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

  Background
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

   	
• NIVI Research (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology (www.isim.ku.dk). 	
• NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.   NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Who are we?
 The Human Organoid facility is a newly established research team within NIVI-R. It conducts independent research projects and runs a Human Organoid facility as a core resource for the research center. We primarily work with upper respiratory and immune organoids, which closely replicate human immune responses to pathogens and vaccines (Wagar, L. et al. Nature Medicine, 2021; Chen, X. & Ghanizada, M. et al. Nature Immunology, 2025). The team's research focus aligns with NIVI-R's overall goal of enhancing our understanding of human immune response and airway immunity. In addition, we will serve as a human organoid facility that collaborates closely with other groups at NIVI-R while continuing to develop organoid systems. The Human Organoid facility has approximately 5 members and is led by Mustafa Ghanizada, MD.

  Homepage:

  If you want to learn more, please visit: www.isim.ku.dk and https://nivi.ku.dk/

  Work assignments:
 The work assignments in the facility are:

   	
• Develop, establish, and maintain iPSC-based human cell and organoid models. 	
• To independently perform predefined research projects using iPSC-derived cell types, organoid models, and other human cell-based systems to address research questions related to human immunity, infection, and airway biology. 	
• To develop, optimize existing protocols, and experiment with new organoid models. 	
• To train people in organoid culture work and basic assays. 	
• To plan and perform experiments in collaboration with the other NIVI-R groups. 	
• To manage the organoid facility (e.g., overview of human sampling cohort, tissue processing, and experiment planning).   Much of the daily work is done independently. The successful candidate will be expected to plan and prioritize activities, coordinate with the facility team and collaborating research groups, troubleshoot unexpected challenges, and implement new experimental workflows.

  We are looking for a staff scientist with the following competencies and experience:

   	
• A person with strong knowledge of cell biology, or a closely related field, with an interest in applying human model systems to understand airway immune responses and respiratory infections. 	
• A person with at least 3 years of documented laboratory experience in advanced human cell culture, preferably involving iPSCs, human primary cells, or tissue-derived models. 	
• Hands-on experience with iPSC culture and/or iPSC-derived cell models, including experience with maintaining, expanding, differentiating, and characterizing iPSCs and/or iPSC-derived cells. 	
• Experience with organoid culture and/or developing 3D human models would be highly beneficial but not required. 	
• Experience with cellular and immunological assays, including immunostaining/imaging, cryo-sectioning, flow cytometry, ELISA, and similar methods. 	
• Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, execute, troubleshoot, and interpret experiments. 	
• Experience in developing, optimizing, and establishing new experimental protocols, with a systematic approach to troubleshooting and improving reproducibility. 	
• Experience working with high-dimensional data and the ability to analyze, interpret, and communicate complex experimental datasets. 	
• An interest in human organoid models and human immunology. 	
• Strong interpersonal skills and an independent, collaborative mindset to support the mission. 	
• Experience in training and supervising students, lab technicians, or junior researchers, as well as in laboratory or facility management. 	
• You have a high degree of drive and pro-activeness with the ability to respond effectively to new tasks and changing priorities in a dynamic, project-driven research environment.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in AI-Driven Optimization of Optical Links based on Nano-Lasers - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
DTU Electro invites applications for a PhD position in AI-driven optimization of optical links based on nano-lasers, within the Villum Investigator program "Power-Efficient Fiber-Optic Communication" (POPCOM) and DNRF Center for NanoPhotonics (NANOPHOTON). The position focuses on developing signaling optimization frameworks to maximize spectral and power efficiency. 

As data-center traffic continues to grow, the energy consumption of optical links has become a critical bottleneck, with power efficiency (measured in J/bit) increasingly rivaling spectral efficiency as a key performance metric. This project will investigate how AI-driven techniques can jointly optimize nano-laser-based transmitters and their waveforms to reduce energy consumption while sustaining high data rates, contributing to more sustainable next-generation optical communication infrastructure. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
We seek a motivated, curious, and outgoing PhD candidate with a solid background in fiber optics, laser-physics, communication engineering, machine learning, and AI-based agentic frameworks. Experience applying machine learning or AI-based optimization frameworks to communication systems and laser modelling, as well as experimental work, is a plus.

The project goal is to develop an AI-driven optimization framework and apply it to realize robust transmitter and receiver architectures that enable power-efficient signaling at the maximum allowable spectral efficiency. The project will cover both algorithm development and experimental implementation.

We offer an opportunity to develop expertise in various domains, including but not limited to:

• Reinforcement learning for the design of optical links
• Development of nano-laser physical system models and data-driven models
• Realization of experimental procedures for testing the developed frameworks
• Building fiber-optic transmission systems
• Investigating transmission performance in practical test-beds
As a PhD candidate at DTU, you will take part in an educational program of 30 ECTS tailored to your needs, covering technical subjects as well as the "soft skills" needed for a successful career in industry or academia.

Your tasks will include research and development of AI-driven methods for mitigating impairments associated with short-range optical links, using energy-efficient signal processing solutions. The overall goal will be to maximize the information rate given the energy-consumption constraint. Specifically, you will focus on the following areas:

• Gradient-based learning for symbol and pulse shaping
• Model-free reinforcement learning strategies for signal pre-distortion
• Physics-informed neural networks
• Maintenance of the GitHub repository for the developed code
• Organizing and managing joint experiments with collaboration groups
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Darko Zibar, dazi@dtu.dk and Professor Jesper Mørk jesm@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU Electro at https://electro.dtu.dk/. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later 1 November, 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. jobs.occupation: Operation Director for SCIENCE Makerspace
jobs.description:
Do you want to create something new? Do you want to fundamentally change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments? Do you want to be part of a unique opportunity in the largest university in Denmark? Then you might be our new SCIENCE Makerspace Operation Director.

  We invite applications for a 5-year position as Operation Director for the SCIENCE Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. The Faculty of Science is committed to sustainably continuing the Makerspace activities at the end of the 5-year period, providing the possibility for extending the position long-term.

   

  About the SCIENCE Makerspace

  We are establishing a top-tier Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen, spearheaded by the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), and the Department of Science Education (IND). The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is built upon a foundation of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) and aims to create an inclusive learning environment that bridges disciplines, supports different ways of learning, and attracts students with diverse backgrounds and interests. Everyone is welcome, and no prior knowledge of makerspaces, machines, or materials is required.

  The SCIENCE Makerspace will be established as a 600 sqm facility centrally located at Nørre Campus, with a budget of 42 million DKK over 5 years supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The Makerspace is expected to host 1-3 university courses per academic quarter, independent projects for BSc/MSc/PhD students, and be a venue for extracurricular workshops and 'blue sky' ideas from faculty and students. The Makerspace will also facilitate the integration between traditional and non-traditional forms of knowledge production within an Expert-in-residence program.

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen is one of Scandinavia's largest science faculties, with over 4,000 staff, ~9,000 students, and an annual turnover exceeding DKK 3 billion, located in the heart of Copenhagen. SCIENCE hosts 12 departments spanning a breadth of disciplines from molecular biology and chemistry to mathematics, computer science, and geoscience, united by a commitment to curiosity-driven, high-impact research. 

   

  Description of the position

  We offer a unique opportunity for you to become the Operation Director of the ‘yet-to-be-build' 600 sqm SCIENCE Makerspace centrally placed at the Northen Campus in Copenhagen. The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is to design, build and run an inclusive and innovative learning space that bridges disciplines, allows for multi-modal learning activities, and attracts a diversified and balanced cohort of students from different educational programs (BSc, MSc, PhD) across the 12 Departments.

  The Operations Director will direct the SCIENCE Makerspace and be the manager for the Makerspace team. The Operation Director is responsible for ensuring that principles for DEIB are mainstreamed in all decisions in the Makerspace. 

  You will be part of the core decision-making on how to organize, establish, and run the ‘one-of-a-kind' Makerspace. You will collaborate with committed faculty from DIKU, NBI, and IND in the establishing phases, and with the Deanery for Education for long-term engagement across the departments in making the Makerspace vision a reality.

  You will be part of hiring the team who will run the makerspace together with you including Technical Lab Manager, Lab Technician, and a group of student mentors.

  This is a unique opportunity to be part of creating something new, in the largest university in Denmark, which fundamentally will change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments.

   

  You will need four core competences to succeed in the position:

   	
• You will need skills and expertise which allow you to strategize and develop ideas which will foster success for the SCIENCE Makerspace vision. This includes the work of identifying and understanding upcoming challenges for e.g. DEIB [DK3] (organizationally, socially, technically, and spatially) and finding solutions, while pro-actively execute required actions. Further, the Operation director must be able to function within an ‘entrepreneurial atmosphere’ where everything is not settled yet. 	
• You will need leadership and management competences which will allow you to lead a mixed Makerspace team of both highly skilled lab manager and lab technicians whose work requires levels of trust and autonomy, as well as student mentors who need clear instructions and guidance. 	
• You will need to navigate and understand the organizational and social structures of academia and university life, this includes considering the intrinsic motivation of researchers/teachers and PhD students, and how they might differ for MSc/BSc students. Such competence can arrive from your own experience during your education and does not require that you have worked in a university setting previously. 	
• You need interest in ‘making’ and Makerspaces. Furthermore, it is important that you consider consulting relevant experts about their views and perspectives, which will allow you to take qualitatively and well-founded decisions about our joint Makerspace.   You will not be a one-person army, instead you will have three main groups with different types of competences and experiences you can draw on in the position, including the Makerspace team, an experienced team of administrative management colleagues, and the Faculty of SCIENCE teaching committee.

  To read more about the vision, plans, and background for the SCIENCE Makerspace, please visit ucphmakerspace.dk

   

  Qualifications

  You are pro-active, find solutions where others see barriers, and are excited about being a core part of establishing, building, and running the brand-new SCIENCE Makerspace at University of Copenhagen, Denmark. 

  You have a relevant higher education or experience from similar positions. 

  You care for students and want to make it possible for all students at SCIENCE to experience learning activities where ‘making’ plays a role, e.g. as part of courses, project work, tech workshops, and extracurricular activities. 

  You are committed to the agenda of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB), know about Universal Design, and strongly believe that all activities and decisions in the pioneer SCIENCE Makerspace must take into account the multiple, intersecting dimensions of groups including, but not limited to genders, internationality, neurodiversity, socioeconomic backgrounds, and physical feasibility.

  Our ideal candidate can be described as:

   	
• Have management experience - potentially from a university or a politically governed organization. 	
• Demonstrates a high degree of trust under responsibility towards our employees, who are self-driven and accountable. As a manager, you help set the overall direction, contribute to daily well-being and cohesion, and support the development of individual employees and the team, while maintaining an overview of strategic initiatives in collaboration with your staff. 	
• Has an understanding of others’ work situations, you are able to develop strong collaborative relationships across employees with different educational and professional backgrounds. 	
• You have personal or professional making experience, pedagogical expertise and DEIB expertise 	
• You are structured, service-minded, approachable, and able to build commitment to strategic decisions. 	
• You thrive in a diverse environment with a wide variety of tasks. 	
• You have collaboration skills and the ability to build networks across professional groups, including across the organization 	
• You have strong communication skills in English (oral and written) and is ready to learn Danish.    

  Living in Copenhagen

  The university is situated in Copenhagen, which is consistently rated among the world's top 10 most livable cities. Located in Denmark, ranked in the top three happiest countries globally, Copenhagen boasts a vibrant culture, rich in music, theater, and community organizations. Life for families is made easier via a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual-career opportunities, maternity/parental leave, and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark. Useful information is also available at the university’s International Staff Mobility (ISM) office, which offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Terms of employment

  The Operation Director reports to the Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm. You will be employed as a senior consultant with managerial responsibility in accordance with the collective agreement for academics in the state sector. There is an opportunity to negotiate additional allowances based on qualifications.

  Note that Denmark protects the economic, social, and physical well-being of its workers, which includes robust health care, childcare, elder care, and other generous benefits. Thus, direct salary comparisons across nations are typically not meaningful.

   

  Further information

  For dedicated information on the new Makerspace, go here: ucphmakerspace.dk

  You are welcome to contact Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm (camillaj@di.ku.dk), or the Academic Director Professor Pernille Bjørn (pernille.bjorn@di.ku.dk) if you have any inquiries about the position.

   

  Filing of application

  As part of the application for the position, please write and submit a 1-page appendix labeled "Core Competences - NAME” in English, where you answer the below questions (one paragraph for each question), considering the description of the position as well as the SCIENCE Makerspace vision, which you can read more about at ucphmakerspace.dk.
 You are not allowed to use AI when writing the appendix. The questions are:

   	
• What is your approach for leadership and management of the SCIENCE Makerspace 	
• What makes you excited about the SCIENCE Makerspace?  	
• What do you expect will be the most challenging part of making the SCIENCE Makerspace vision a reality?   Please submit your application, including appendix, CV and relevant documentation, electronically via the Job Portal (click the link “APPLY FOR THE POSITION” at the bottom of the advertisement), so that it reaches us no later than 14 November 2026. We expect to hold interviews on 27 November 2026 and 4 December 2026.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion, or sexual orientation. Appointments will be based solely on qualifications.
